method: candidate lines proposed by corridor detection; identity decided from printed address runs
why_not_one_block_off: Contrary to the keymap note, both sheets do letter this corridor in the roadway. Sheet 16 prints 'AVE. D. OR MARKET' vertically in it on view 1 (native ~1160) and again on view 2; sheet 67 prints 'AVE. D OR MARKET' in it on view 2 (native ~2189) and again on view 3, with the printed 70' width label inside the same corridor on both. The hundred-block runs settle it independently on each sheet, the address series restarting at each lettered avenue (B/Strand=200, C=300, D=400, E=500, F=600). Sheet 16: the block west of the chosen corridor carries 301-323 odd / 302-324 even along 31st and 32nd Sts (300 block) and the block east of it carries 401-423 / 402-424 (400 block); the next corridor west is lettered 'AVE. C OR MECHANIC' (view 1, native ~156) and the next east is 'AVE. E. OR POST OFFICE' (native 2169.3), east of which view 3 shows the 500 block running 501-523 / 502-524 up to 'AVE. F. OR CHURCH' (~3168). Sheet 67: identical break - 301-323 / 302-324 west of the chosen corridor, 401-423 / 402-424 east of it; the next corridor west is 'AVE. C OR MECHANIC' (native ~1184), west of which view 1 shows the 200 block 201-223 / 202-224 running back to 'AVE. B OR STRAND' (~147), and the next east is 'AVE. E OR POST OFFICE' (~3190). So the avenue one block west (Ave C, Mechanic) is excluded on both sheets because it is the line that breaks 200 from 300, and the avenue one block east (Ave E, Post Office) is excluded because it breaks 400 from 500; only Ave D breaks 300 from 400 on both. Near-equal native x was deliberately not used, and here it is doubly misleading: sheet 16's Ave D (1159.9) sits only ~25 px from sheet 67's Ave C (~1184), and sheet 16's Ave E (2169.3) sits only ~20 px from sheet 67's Ave D (2188.6), so an x-proximity match would have tied D to C or E to D and sheared this row by a full block. The two plates are offset by almost exactly one avenue: sheet 16 runs C-D-E-F at ~156 / 1159.9 / 2169.3 / ~3168 while sheet 67 runs B-C-D-E at ~147 / ~1184 / 2188.6 / ~3190. Current mosaic coordinates were likewise not used. The red position marker was ignored; it falls inside blocks and on rail sidings, and the 20 ft dashed 6" W. PIPE alleys in this district measure ~60 native px against ~208 native px for the avenue roadway and change no address hundred. MEASUREMENT: Native x is the roadway CENTRELINE, the midpoint of the two block street-casing lines, located to sub-pixel precision by an intensity-weighted centroid with a per-row adaptive ink threshold, read against the green native-pixel ruler (calibration verified on every crop: the labelled long ticks land within 1 px of exact multiples of 500). This is the dock/warehouse quadrant, where railroad sidings are drawn as pairs of rails inside the avenue roadways, so the casings were pinned at the block corners at 32nd/33rd Sts and measured in row bands clear of the rails, not by blind line detection. Sheet 16 Ave D casings: west 1055.6 (view 2) / 1055.0 (view 1), east 1264.2 / 1264.3 -> centre 1159.8, roadway width 209.0 native px = 69.0 ft. Sheet 67 Ave D casings: west 2085.3 (view 3) / 2085.4 (view 2), east 2292.6 / 2293.3 -> centre 2189.1, width 207.8 native px = 68.6 ft; the printed 70' label sits between them. Consistency check on the identification: the sheet-16-minus-sheet-67 offset is -1029.3 px on the Ave D centreline and -1028.4 px on the Ave C east casing (sheet 16 260.0, sheet 67 1288.4), agreeing to 0.9 px; a one-avenue misidentification would have moved one of these by ~1000 px. Note sheet 67's scan is markedly darker (paper luminance ~165 vs ~180 on sheet 16), so a fixed ink threshold marks its paper as ink; all measurements used a per-row adaptive threshold.
